author: jdholtz
body:
Since Python 3.8 has officially reached its EOL, support for it is dropped. Additionally, official support for Python 3.13 has been added. Here is a list of specific changes done:
- Built-in types are now used instead of importing them from typing (Dict, List, Tuple) which was added in Python 3.9
- The pytz dependency is removed in favor of the built-in `zoneinfo` module

I have not found a way to upgrade the Dockerfile past `python:3.12-rc-alpine`. If it goes past this tag, the webdriver times out. If I instead switch to an Ubuntu image with `python:3.13-slim`, the script is detected very often. We'll have to stay at an old version until we can figure this out.

author: mhucka
body: The `setup.py` files (at the top level as well as the various Cirq modules) currently define the `author` and `author_email` fields. The set of authors of Cirq, and the set of maintainers of Cirq at any given time, are somewhat overlapping but not identical. The [Python Packaging User Guide](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/core-metadata/#maintainer) defines `maintainer` and `maintainer_email` fields to identify the maintainer contact info. This PR adds the values to the `setup.py` files.

author: tomasruizt
body:
The user can have a multi-turn conversation with the model.
* I changed the interface of the model. Rather than a single `prompt`, it gets a list of `messages` as a JSON input. These `messages` are parsed into a full conversation. If we wanted to preserve the existing interface for backward compatibility, we could add `messages` as an optional parameter that overwrites the `prompt`.
* I tried using a pydantic model directly in the `predict()` method, but pydantic types are not yet allowed, so the function accepts `messages` as a string and parses it within the `predict()` method
* I removed the `cleanup()` method, because it seems unnecessary, but I have no strong opinions about this.

author: chinmayshringi
body:
## Description

This PR implements comprehensive syscall handling in the RawPOSIX dispatcher, focusing on security and memory safety. Each syscall implementation has been carefully compared against its NaCl counterpart to ensure consistent behavior while leveraging Rust's safety features.

Key improvements include:
- Enhanced memory validation using Rust's type system
- Proper protection flags for memory access (READ/WRITE)
- Consistent error handling with POSIX-compliant errno codes
- Resource management at cage layer

Reference NaCl implementation: [nacl_syscall_common.c](https://github.com/Lind-Project/native_client/blob/5f51b67716d15133ec41f8180ab779d527141a75/src/trusted/service_runtime/nacl_syscall_common.c#L801)

- `cargo build` - Verifies compilation and type safety
- Manual verification against NaCl implementation

author: ltamasi
body:
Summary:
The patch is the read-side counterpart of https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/pull/13197 . It adds support for K-nearest-neighbor vector similarity searches to `FaissIVFIndex`. There are two main pieces to this:

1) `KNNIterator` is an `Iterator` implementation that is returned by `FaissIVFIndex` upon a call to `NewIterator`. `KNNIterator` treats its `Seek` target as a vector embedding and passes it to FAISS along with the number of neighbors requested `k` as well as the number of probes to use (i.e. the number of inverted lists to check). Applications can then use `Next` (and `Prev`) to iterate over the the vectors in the result set. `KNNIterator` exposes the primary keys associated with the result vectors (see below how this is done), while `value` and `columns` are empty. The iterator also supports a property `rocksdb.faiss.ivf.index.distance` that can be used to retrieve the distance/similarity metric for the current result vector.
2) `IteratorAdapter` takes a RocksDB secondary index iterator (see https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/pull/13257) and adapts it to the interface required by FAISS (`faiss::InvertedListsIterator`), enabling FAISS to read the inverted lists stored in RocksDB. Since FAISS only supports numerical vector ids of type `faiss::idx_t`, `IteratorAdapter` uses `KNNIterator` to assign ephemeral (per-query) ids to the inverted list items read during iteration, which are later mapped back to the original primary keys by `KNNIterator`.

Differential Revision: D67684898

author: stxticovfl
body:
This PR lays out a general structure to begin the process of *compiler optimizations*. Currently, two optimization funcs have been added, both having the same arguments:
- `CheckPrefixOptimize` is called after a prefix function from a rule, intaking the code position before any modifications to the compiled code (e.g. by the prefix function or by another optimization), the amount of constants before any modifications to the compiled code, and the function called to check how to optimize it. Currently supports the `GetInteger` and `GetUnary` prefix functions.
- `CheckInfixOptimize` does the same exact thing but for infix functions. Currently supports the `GetBinary` infix function.

This PR also adds a helper function `Compiler::GetTotalOpcodeSize`, used by `CheckInfixOptimize` and the debug functions. It also adds a `IS_NUMBER` check to `BITWISE_NOT` (which I imagine was definitely supposed to have it) and does the tiniest of optimizations changing a `* 2` to a `<< 1` (which the compiler probably made into a `<< 1` anyway but I kept it in this PR just because I had already took an eye to it before.)

author: wunkolo
body:
Allocates the correct amount of UBOs and Image Samplers ahead of time.

Thank you for the Vulkan implementation. I did some testing and ran into a crash and validation error regarding the global descriptor-pool here not declaring enough descriptors of certain types ahead of time.

This addresses the issue directly, but a more robust solution might be needed here later on. This is enough to get all of the tests to run without any crashes on my system or validation _errors_ in particular, though I do get an allocation error involving the application reaching the maximum amount of allocations(4096 on this system) when running `FunnelTest` in particular. That will probably need a whole new allocation strategy though to sub-allocate out of a larger heap of VkDeviceMemory rather than allocating a new one for each DebugDraw TriangleBatch.

For reference, I tested on my ThinkPad X13S(Windows on ARM, Native Vulkan driver) and got valdation messages like this followed by a crash due to the global descriptor pool only allocating space for a `cFrameCount`-amount of uniform-buffers despite there being descriptor-layouts that want two uniform-buffers each descriptor set or one singular texture sampler per-set:

```
VK: Validation Error: [ VUID-VkDescriptorSetAllocateInfo-apiVersion-07896 ] Object 0: handle = 0x27d60e0000000019, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_POOL; | MessageID = 0x5584bd53 | vkAllocateDescriptorSets():  Unable to allocate 1 descriptors of type VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER from VkDescriptorPool 0x27d60e0000000019[]. This pool only has 0 descriptors of this type remaining. The Vulkan spec states: If the VK_KHR_maintenance1 extension is not enabled and VkPhysicalDeviceProperties::apiVersion is less than Vulkan 1.1, descriptorPool must have enough free descriptor capacity remaining to allocate the descriptor sets of the specified layouts (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.290.0/mac/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkDescriptorSetAllocateInfo-apiVersion-07896)
```

body:
- **Context:** This change introduces a concrete implementation of the `ParamConfig` interface, `SmaRsiParamConfig`, specifically for configuring and optimizing parameters of the SMA/RSI trading strategy. This provides a dedicated configuration for this specific strategy.
- **Changes:**
    - Created `src/main/java/com/verlumen/tradestream/backtesting/params/SmaRsiParamConfig.java`: Implements `ParamConfig` to define chromosome specifications and parameter creation logic for the SMA/RSI strategy. It specifies integer ranges for moving average and RSI periods, and double ranges for overbought and oversold thresholds.
    - Created `src/test/java/com/verlumen/tradestream/backtesting/params/BUILD`: Defines the build target for the unit tests of `SmaRsiParamConfig`.
    - Created `src/test/java/com/verlumen/tradestream/backtesting/params/SmaRsiParamConfigTest.java`: Contains unit tests to verify the correct configuration and parameter creation logic of `SmaRsiParamConfig`.
    - Modified `src/main/java/com/verlumen/tradestream/backtesting/params/BUILD`: Added a dependency on the `//protos:strategies_java_proto` to the `params_lib` target.
- **Benefits:**
    - Provides a dedicated and well-defined way to configure and optimize SMA/RSI strategy parameters during backtesting.
    - Improves code organization and maintainability by separating strategy-specific parameter configuration.
    - Introduces unit tests to ensure the correctness of the SMA/RSI parameter configuration.

author: djahandarie
body:
In https://github.com/yomidevs/yomitan/pull/1676 we merged a change that completely broke all popups.

Our E2E testing (playwright) did detect the issue, but its output was ignored.

My analysis is that it was ignored because the output of `playwright-report-summary`:
1. does not make a clear visual differentiation between flaky tests and failures, requiring the user to carefully analyze the output
2. does not link to the report artifact, making it high friction for the user to actually check the report to see what changed
3. does not have a clear call to action instructing the user what they should do

I believe it is better to have our own custom comments (basically revert https://github.com/yomidevs/yomitan/pull/1543 and improve the original comments a bit to properly differentiate between flaky and failure). That is what this PR does.

This achieves:
* Very small comment size, with just a single icon, making it easy to read and interpret
* Clear call to action to user instructing them what to do based on results
* Low friction via a direct link to the playwright-report (made possible by the new v4 artifact system on GitHub)
* Proper differentiate between flaky and failure, choosing to interpret flaky as :heavy_check_mark: (but still comment to instruct user to improve tests) and failure as :warning: so it's hard to miss.

author: dsharlet
body:
- `depends_on` previously would track the dependencies of every buffer it finds in the IR, even if the caller didn't care about them. This PR fixes it to only track dependencies that we either care about, or shadow something we do care about.
- `substitute` did some minor extra work when substitutions are affected by implicit bounds.

This pull request introduces improvements to our authentication routes and CORS middleware configuration. Here are the key updates:

### Key Changes:

1. **Authentication Route Enhancements**:
   - Added new redirect handlers for both local and third-party logins in `auth.routes.js`.
   - This change streamlines response management, providing a more consistent and efficient handling of authentication processes.

2. **CORS Middleware Formatting**:
   - Improved the formatting of CORS middleware in `server.js` for better readability and consistency.
   - This change enhances code maintainability and makes it easier for developers to understand and modify CORS settings if needed.

The primary motivation for these changes is to improve the overall structure and efficiency of our authentication system while also enhancing the readability of our server configuration. By streamlining our redirect handlers, we aim to provide a more robust and consistent user experience during the login process, regardless of the authentication method used.

This pull request includes changes to the `settlement.model.ts` file to clean up imports, improve code readability, and enhance schema validation for the `settlement` model. The most important changes include consolidating imports, reformatting model definitions, and adding validation constraints to schema fields.

Code cleanup and readability improvements:

* Consolidated imports in `src/db/schemas/settlement.model.ts` to a single line.
* Reformatted `senderId` and `receiverId` definitions in the `settlementModel` to a single line each.

Schema validation enhancements:

* Added `.min(60)` and `.max(60)` validation constraints to `senderId`, `receiverId`, and `groupId` fields in the `selectSettlementSchema`.
* Added `.min(60)` and `.max(60)` validation constraints to `senderId`, `receiverId`, and `groupId` fields in the `insertSettlementSchema`.

author: lihanchen2004
body:
The code snippet:

```cpp
std::string name = clazz.c_str();
```
is redundant and unnecessary when initializing a `std::string` object. 

The method `std::string::operator=(const char*)`, which takes a C-style string (`const char*`), introduces an extra conversion step when the input is already a `std::string`. Specifically, the `c_str()` method is used to extract a `const char*` pointer from `clazz`, and then `std::string` reconstructs the string from the pointer.

Instead, the simpler and more efficient approach is:

```cpp
std::string name = clazz;
```

This directly utilizes the copy constructor or move constructor of `std::string`, avoiding the unnecessary intermediate conversion to `const char*`. It results in cleaner, more idiomatic C++ code with no performance penalty.

Addresses: https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2717

author: lossydragon
body:
### Description
Testing a project on an Android device (Google Pixel 3 XL) running Android 12 (SP1A.210812.016.C1) and caught ByteArrayOutputStream#toString() throwing NoSuchMethodError with JavaSteam and the project compiled to JDK11. 

Lowering the bytecode to 1.8 on the project to let desugaring take over had no effect. 

Android 12 should support Java 11, but something may have not been implemented on this device to be supported. 
See https://developer.android.com/build/jdks#compileSdk

This PR replaced baos.toString() to the String alternative, which works fine now.

Edit: 
Also fixes compatibility issues with InputStream.readNBytes()

Closes #307

author: thanasipantazides
body:
Add some preliminary scripts for MSFC optic effective area plotting.

I know already there are some hardcoded paths that will break when anyone else runs, this is just the quickest way to spread around access to these codes. 

Start in optics-tools-py/examples/foxsi4_msfc_ea.py, and run it with a single additional argument: a path to a folder where you want plots saved. 

A `dict` is created at the top of these example files to hold paths to the data you want to reference. Some examples plot multiple optics, and for each optic there may be multiple files of calibration data to use, including background measurements. As written, these presume you have a folder above your current one called `data/`, and you store optic calibration data in there under folders named for each flight optic `fm1`, `fm2`, and `fm3`. So you may need to edit these `dict`s to point at your real data.

Depends on:
- `scipy`
- `astropy`
- `numpy`
- `matplotlib`

The RangeMap.gaps() function previously iterated
over all ranges prior to the query range before
returning the first overlapping gap. This results
in a worst-case O(n) time complexity per query.

Now the gaps() function reuses the overlaps() code to
get an iterator to the first overlapping range in O(log(n)) time.

Fixes issue #103.

author: priya2698
body:
This PR modifies the `hasTrivialAllocationDomain` to consider if the tensorview has a DID loop split. In this case, we compare the corresponding iterdomains for logical and allocation domain across all but the sharded logical axis.

Note: This does not guarantee that `MatmulOp` with non-trivial stride order will work for DID loop split. I suspect it will require some additional changes to the `MatmulOp::evaluate` method.

author: halfwhitt
body:
Except for two spots that handle RTL text direction, the `_layout_row_children` and `_layout_column_children` methods of Pack are identical, swapping out the relevant names of width for height, top/bottom for left/right, etc. I'm impressed by the almost total lack of drift between two methods of 200+ lines each, but it would be easier to update and modify the layout mechanism if changes could be made in just one place. This PR combines both methods into one, `_layout_children`, that ~~accepts a `direction` parameter~~ uses `node.style.direction` to determine the main and cross axes.

My first pass at this involved a lot of ungainly `getattr`. To make the spellings clearer, I've added some convenience methods to `Box` and `IntrinsicSize` that accept the dimension name as a string, like so:

- `node.layout.content_height` -> `node.layout.content("height")`
- `node.intrinsic.height` -> `node.intrinsic.dim("height")`

I'm not at all married to these spellings, they just seemed intuitive.

author: mrexodia
body:
- The `page.executed` assignment is moved to after the check, since we might exit early here and then incorrectly mark non-executable code as executed.
- Do not check for `perm::READ` in `ensure_executable` (this is what adds support)
- Do not modify the permissions when detecting self-modifying code, only add `perm::IN_CODE_CACHE` (since this is already checked in `write_physical -> check_self_modifying_write`)

Some open issues to potentially handle later:
- Introduce a new `MemError::ExecUninitialized` and propagate this up from `ensure_exec` (requires more significant changes). The reason for this is that executing uninitialized code will return a confusing error to the user
- There is a bug where stepping over a single-byte `nop` instruction triggers the `ExecUninitialized` state (still needs more investigation)
- There might be a bug that allows reading from a zero execute-only page regardless of the permissions (also needs more investigation)

The widget target will attempt to import the SWIFT_OBJC_BRIDGING_HEADER (Bridging-Header.h) that is not built yet. It leads to the compile error. author: shahar-y
body:
This PR addresses #1656 found by @MissFreedom where the max_iter does not force ending of the agent iteration in trying to solve the task. 

The problem was that the first time the loop reaches the condition of `_should_force_answer`, the value of `self.have_forced_answer` is changed to `True`:
```python
if self._should_force_answer():
    if self.have_forced_answer:
        return AgentFinish(
            thought="",
            output=self._i18n.errors(
                "force_final_answer_error"
            ).format(formatted_answer.text),
            text=formatted_answer.text,
        )
```


But then because the code of `_should_force_answer` contains the condition: 

```python
    def _should_force_answer(self) -> bool:
        """Determine if a forced answer is required based on iteration count."""
        return (self.iterations >= self.max_iter) and not self.have_forced_answer
```

Then `_should_force_answer` will never return `True` again as ` self.have_forced_answer` is True.

Therefore, I simply removed `and not self.have_forced_answer` from the condition since it has no meaning, and the new function is: 

```python
    def _should_force_answer(self) -> bool:
        """Determine if a forced answer is required based on iteration count."""
        return self.iterations >= self.max_iter
```

body:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a3d0b1c-12c5-4d54-9f95-09eb303ac4f5)

## About the PR
The shadow anomaly is now a portal to the shadow dimension.
The shadow dimension is a dangerous place full of valuable items, salvage loot and chasms. (There are currently no monsters or specialised shadow loot here as it's out of scope)
You can easily exit the shadow dimension by entering one of the many random one-way shadow portals. This also allows you to use the shadow dimension to penetrate protected locations on the station

The shadow haze from the anomaly no longer creates random shadow rifts.

It's a pretty empty location at the moment, but it's a basic C# baseline that can easily be developed by YML
expected directions for future development:
- special shadow plants and seeds for hydroponics
- special shadow loot
- A T3 technology that allows you to open stable portals to the shadow dimension.
- special dangerous monsters that can't be fought with normal weapons.
- new dimension types?

## Why / Balance
approved and discussed among maintainers

## Technical details
<!-- Summary of code changes for easier review. -->
A new ‘Alternate Realities’ system has been added. This system allows you to generate alternative versions of grids.
Let's examine the prototype file of the alternate dimension:
```yml
- type: alternateDimension
  id: Shadowlands
  defaultTile: FloorChromite #the dimension will completely replicate the shape of the original grid using this type of tile
  mapComponents: #all components to be added to the alternative dimension map. You can customise parallax, atmosphere, global illumination, weather, and anything else you need.
  - type: Parallax
    parallax: Darkness
  gridComponents: #all components that will be added to the alternate dimension grid. For example, gravity.
  - type: Gravity
    enabled: true
    inherent: true
  replacements: #Pairs from tags and EntProtoId. During generation, if there is an entity with one of the specified tags on the main grid, it will create the specified entity on the same coordinates in the alt-reality.
    Wall: ShadowDimensionBarrierSpawner
    Window: ShadowDimensionFillSpawner
    Pipe: ShadowDimensionFillSpawner
    Table: TableStoneChromite
    # Loot zone
    ShadowSideLoot: ShadowDimensionLootSpawner
    ShadowSideLootEpic: ShadowDimensionEpicLootSpawner
```
Currently, the system is only used during station initialisation: selecting one of a randomly listed alternative dimension, and creating it for the largest station grid.

As you can understand, this system is extremely easy to extend, and you can easily create new kinds of alternative versions of grids. 

```yml
- type: entity
  id: BaseStationAlternateDimension
  abstract: true
  components:
    - type: StationAlternateDimensionGenerator
      dimensions: 
      - Shadowlands
```
All of this works in tandem with the new component

```yml
  - type: AlternateDimensionAutoPortal
    otherSidePortal: PortalBlue
    targetDimension: Shadowlands
```

This component, when initialising an entity, looks for the alterative dimension of the grid and the corresponding coordinates. At this point, it creates a pair of entities specified in the component and automatically links them together. This is used for the portal system. So ‘Shadow rift’ portals from a shadow anomaly that used to teleport within a random radius now teleport IN, or OUT of the shadow dimension, depending on where they are located.

body:
- **Context:** This change relaxes the generic type constraint on the `ChromosomeSpec` interface to better accommodate various numeric types supported by Jenetics.
- **Changes:**
    - Updated the generic type parameter `T` of `ChromosomeSpec` from `T extends Comparable<T>` to `T extends Number & Comparable<? super T>`. This allows `ChromosomeSpec` to work with subtypes of `Number`.
    - The `DoubleChromosomeSpec` and `IntegerChromosomeSpec` implementations are now `final` and have reduced visibility (package-private).
    - The `createChromosome()` method in `ChromosomeSpec` now returns `NumericChromosome<T, ?>` instead of `Chromosome<? extends Gene<T, ?>>`.
- **Benefits:**
    - Improves compatibility with Jenetics' `NumericChromosome` and `NumericGene` hierarchy.
    - Provides more flexibility in defining chromosome specifications for different numeric parameter types.
    - Enhances the type safety of parameter configuration by aligning with Jenetics' type system.

body:
* Added tracing instrumentation on TableContext methods from ActivitySource `"FSharp.AWS.DynamoDB"`. This is roughly in line with the published [semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/database/dynamodb/)
* Added a dependency on `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource` - have seen reports that this won’t build on some `netstandard2.0` platforms (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/issues/3448). I’ve specified 6.0.0 which should work but may cause version conflicts(?)
* Added a dependency on `System.Text.Json`, purely for (the questionable utility of) tagging consumed capacity as an array of JSON strings as recommended. I’m unsure how to properly add this for netstandard libs.
* I’ve not attempted to log exceptions from within the TableContext, just the AWS client calls.
* No Metric support - the only finalised DB metric is [`db.client.operation.duration`](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/database/database-metrics/#metric-dbclientoperationduration) which will need a stopwatch around all the client calls. Recording consumed capacity as a metric is probably the more useful value.
* Started work on adding recorded activities to the test TableFixture but this needs actual assertions.

Added support for device mapping in Paged Attention by passing the device list from the mapper to the cache engine. Manual moving was required for certain unmapped tensors in the paged attention forward pass. I have tested the device mapping support on several text models and it appears to be functional. 

Memory allocation is currently calculated as if all memory is available on a single device, resulting in that memory being split across devices; ideally, we should calculate available memory per GPU. If this PR is fine, I will work on this next.

Additionally, this feature currently only supports GPU devices due to an error when attempting to use reshape_and_cache() with non-cuda tensors.  

Please let me know if you'd like me to revise anything!

_Introduced a dynamic block to the Kubernetes module to conditionally configure either a System Assigned Managed Identity or a Service Principal for the AKS cluster based on the identity_or_sp variable._

* If authentication_method is set to "identity", the module configures a SystemAssigned managed identity.

* If authentication_method is set to "service_principal", the module configures a service_principal block using the provided client_id and client_secret.

* client_id and client_secret are pulled from keyvault using data "azurerm_keyvault_secret" blocks

* on using identity, Only SystemAssigned managed identity is used, ~~Not user assigned managed identity~~

**This update ensures flexibility in choosing the authentication method for the AKS cluster.**

Code like this

This PR tries to remove most hard coding of a particular integer size to make the package work and easy to use on 32 bit platforms.

body:
* libxmp failed to load some modules as it applied the 16-bit and loop flags to samples incorrectly (background.liq, free mind.liq, lite.liq, part of the sky.liq).
* libxmp incorrectly bounded note events, causing some modules to fail to load (flush.liq, free mind.liq, lite.liq).
* libxmp incorrectly converted volume events (off-by-one).
* Add support for stereo samples and bidirectional loops.
* The default channel volume and pan tables were ignored in format 0.00 modules.
* Fix LDSS 1.01+ instrument global volume.
* Use mix volume to simulate LIQ's gaining channel volume and instrument global volume fields.
* Fix effect Gxx Global Volume. Values >64 are not supported yet.
* Misc. cleanup.
* Revert modifications to both Liquid Tracker loaders' volslide effects (wasn't aware libxmp was already handling that in the regular volslide implementation).
* Debug: fixed printing of unpacked event effects (was converting prior to output).
* Debug: fixed printing of sample loop flag.

All known LIQs (including the new one I made with a converter...) load now, though there are some misc. effects differences I didn't bother addressing. Yet another patch split off of the loop modes patch that got too big and I had to make tools and a test module for :(

author: fintasticman
body:
This fixes almost all the C99 compliance issues in the implementation of Clay.

Now the only issues remaining are:
- [x] `##__VA_ARGS__` (and related), which isn't easy to solve without switching to C23.
- [x] Defining a struct within `offsetof` to get the alignment of a type, which also isn't easy to solve without switching to C11. (Solved using macro magic)
- [ ] A number of times that signed integers are compared with unsigned integers, which will need some rethinking of all the types for lengths and indices etc.
- [ ] Some strangeness with the `CLAY_SIZING_FIT` and `CLAY_SIZING_GROW` macros, which don't compile without specifying `-std=gnu99` rather than `-std=c99` for some reason.
- [ ] (The compiler warning on GCC discussed below. Not actually standards-non-compliant, but it does complain.)

author: sasa-tomic
body:
### Summary of Changes

This commit introduces a custom panic hook that gracefully handles panics in the application, enhancing the user experience in case of errors. Additionally, it streamlines the terminal handling by removing unnecessary mutable references during rendering.

### Details of Changes:

- **Panic Hook**: Added a custom panic hook to safely disable raw mode and show the cursor before invoking the default panic handler. This ensures that the terminal state is correctly restored on panic.

- **Terminal Handling**: Refactored the code to remove mutable references (e.g., `&mut terminal`) in function calls where it wasn't necessary. This improves code readability and reduces potential mutability issues.

- **Async Run Function**: Introduced a new async function `run` to encapsulate the main logic of the application, making the main function more concise and focused.

- **Error Handling Messages**: Enhanced error messages for various checks related to the environment variable `OPENAI_KEY` and upstream branch determination, maintaining user awareness of the application status.

### Additional Notes:

- There are no breaking changes introduced in this update. All existing functionalities remain intact.

body: This pull request introduces a WebSocket communication system between the Flask backend and the React frontend to provide real-time updates on the cloning process. The implementation utilizes Flask-SocketIO on the backend and Socket.IO on the frontend to transmit periodic progress updates, including the percentage of completion. The React UI dynamically displays the cloning progress, enhancing the user experience with seamless feedback. Additionally, error handling mechanisms are implemented to manage potential connection issues. Future improvements may include more granular progress reporting and more sophisticated error handling.

#### Summary

The transformer object passed to the `TransformStream` constructor can now also have a `cancel` method, which is called whenever the readable side is cancelled or when the writable side is aborted. See [the specification](https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-transformer-cancel) and [the spec change](https://github.com/whatwg/streams/pull/1283) for context.

#### Test results and supporting details

This method is not yet supported in any browser. However, server runtimes such as Node.js and Deno already support it:
* Node.js: implemented in https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/3dd96f1fabf39661dcebd4f3677c76d9a670e04e, shipped in [version 20.14.0](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v20.14.0)
* Deno: implemented in https://github.com/denoland/deno/commit/6450334f5bbb059b55005cebfef57fa7969b625e, shipped in [version 1.38.0](https://github.com/denoland/deno/releases/tag/v1.38.0)

author: belfdev
body:
### Task Management Feature

**Overview:**
This PR introduces a _task management feature_ to our application, allowing users to create, update, delete, and manage tasks effectively.

**Key Features:**
- **Task Creation:** Users can create tasks with essential attributes such as title, description, assignees, and status.
- **Task Retrieval:** Users can retrieve tasks by ID and view all tasks associated with their account.
- **Task Updates:** Users can update existing tasks, including modifying titles, descriptions, and assignees. The `created_by` field is protected to ensure that it cannot be altered after task creation.
- **Task Deletion:** Users can delete tasks they have created, with appropriate authorization checks to prevent unauthorized deletions.
- **Assignee Management:** Users can assign multiple users to tasks, enhancing collaboration and task tracking.

**Testing:**
- Added unit tests to cover all aspects of task management, including:
  - Successful task creation, updates, and deletions.
  - Handling of unauthorized access and validation errors.
  - Ensuring that tasks can only be deleted by their authors.

author: ceigey
body:
When you select the tab for installing Elysia for Node in the quick start guide, the first instruction to install Node accidentally has the following text:

> You can install Bun with the command below:

This replaces the reference to "Bun" with "Node.js", to be consistent with the code snippet below installing Node.js with Brew.

```diff
- You can install Bun with the command below:
+ You can install Node.js with the command below:
```

In addition, the next section has two different tabs, one for TS and one for JS. If you select the JS one, it warns you:

> Using Elysia with TypeScript will miss out on some features auto-completion, advanced type checking and end-to-end type safety which is the core feature of Elysia.

author: breadhunt
body:
## About The Pull Request

Merges FC and SL prep into one, complete with a drawable map table for group planning

Moves minimap tablet from CIC to the FC/SL preps on each ship to encourage use more

## Pillar of Spring:
(Note: Pictures outdated; minimap tablet is on the FC vendor in each of these photos)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9095da8c-d609-4778-81eb-bda657449871)

This also gives room for more spacious medic/engi/SG preps on Pillar of Spring specifically:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75c0e026-b42c-42c9-a1df-be9d78bf9198)

## Arachne: (fire alarm fixed)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6af38813-002e-42ab-a98c-5ab2f36d7baf)

## Sulaco:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ce9636d-aacc-433b-a9a7-807550e4cc38)

## Theseus:
Theseus has SL prep split by squad. Because of this Theseus instead has a minimap briefing room outside the FC office:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15891aa8-20fd-415c-a45c-582589132936)
## Why It's Good For The Game

FCs and SLs need to work and plan together to ensure the marines' victory but the rooms they prepare in are often completely across the ship. This is bad for several reasons:
- FC/SLs can't plan during the first minutes of drop, which is the only time you get before engis/etc already have their gear setup.
- It's harder to plan over comms, it's easier in-person. It's even easier with a minimap table beside you.
- If you want to draft a plan on tacmap you previously had to walk all the way over to CIC and waste like 10 minutes waiting for everyone to arrive. Now you can hold a meeting from the comfort of prep, visually show your plan to the SLs, then draw it up!
- People tend to work together better if they've "met in person". Higher chance of meeting in person = higher cohesion = cooler gameplay.
- War room meetings are cool and I think we should make them easier to do
## Changelog
:cl:
add: Merged FC and SL prep rooms on Arachne, Sulaco and Pillar of Spring. Added a minimap table war room outside the FC's office on Theseus.
add: Expanded Pillar of Spring engineer, medic and smartgunner prep rooms.
/:cl:

- Since `Map.of()` can accept at most 10 KV entries, and pale oak leaves are the 11th entry, the `leavesData` map is now populated in the `onInitializeClient()` method by adding each KV entry one by one. `LeafData` for the pale oak leaves is set to `null` to prevent Particular from spawning any leaf particles on them since vanilla already has leaf particles for them, much like cherry blossom leaves.

author: rokm
body:
Clean-up of the test suite, with the following highlights:

1. Make `psutil` optional. This means that if a test times out, we cannot properly clean the process tree (i.e., first kill the child and grandchild processes, and only then kill the parent), but at least that way we can run the test suite on platforms where `psutil` is unavailable. In the absence of `psutil`, the `pyi_builder` fixture now automatically skips interactive tests (the ones that set `runtime` argument).

2. Revise the text messages emitted by `pyi_builder` during different stages; ensure they are always written to both stdout and stderr, so that they show up in pytest's captured stdout / stderr sections; although at the cost of them appearing twice when capture is turned off (i.e., `pytest -s ...`). Add an `[APP-BUILDER:{step_name}]` prefix to easily identify the source of the message (and distinguish it from the bootloader and from the python part of the test program). When running the test executable, do not redirect stdout and stderr to pipes; this way, when capture is turned off, we can see the messages from bootloader "in real-time", instead of them being dumped to output once the subprocess finishes (that is, if the `Popen.communicate` call succeeds). I'm not sure why we had this redirect in the first place, but it is worth noting that several tests run the executable outside of this fixture using `subprocess.Popen()` and without redirecting output streams...

3. Have the `ctypes_dylib` fixture use `distutils` to compile the custom shared library used in `ctypes`-based tests (as opposed to hard-coded compiler command strings). Make this fixture session-scoped so that we compile the test shared library only once per test session, instead of for every test. Remove the `skipif_compiler_unavailable`; the `ctypes_dylib` fixture now skips the test if compilation fails.

4. Replace the use of legacy `tmpdir` fixture (based on `py.path.local` with `tmp_path` (based on `pathlib.Path`). Disable the legacypath pytest plugin in setup.cfg to enforce transition. Update our own fixtures to use `pathlib.Path`, and propagate its use throughout the test suite (e.g., use the `/` operator to construct paths instead of using `os.path.join` wherever possible).

5. Attempt to replace `str.format()` and `%`-based formatting with f-strings wherever possible.

6. Remove unused `tests/speed` and `tests/scripts` directories.

7. Move files from `tests/functional/test_hooks` into `test/functional` directory. Collect some of the tests into their own test_*.py file. Inline some of the more trivial test scripts. Closes #7930 (as it goes in the opposite direction - see https://github.com/pyinstaller/pyinstaller/pull/7930#issuecomment-1721022631).

8. Remove the `pyi_testmod_gettemp` and `pyi_get_datadir` modules that were used by some test programs to infer the location of their temporary directory and/or temporary data directory. It usually makes more sense to either bundle the said data into the test application, or pass the path to it via command-line argument. This also  prevents tests from appearing to have an unused `tmp_path` or `data_dir` fixture.

9. Remove the coding marker from the couple of files that still have it (throughout the whole codebase, not just tests).

10. Consistently use "macOS" instead of MacOS", "Mac OS", "Mac OS X", "Mac OSX", "OS X", and "OSX" (throughout the whole codebase).

author: leonardoarcari
body:
## Description

Chakra UI with the v3 version has broken everything and after a few hours of swearing I discovered that it is incompatible with TailwindCSS. Furthermore, the documentation is still particularly poor. Now, since this is a side-project, thinking of rewriting every component in Chakra just to be able to migrate to the new stable is out of the question. Given that we will have at most 3 components migrated to Chakra, I would be in favor of saying goodbye to the framework.

Among the libraries shared by @corradopetrelli, there is one that seems to be right for us: https://ui.shadcn.com/

In short, it is based on Radix UI (very big project) but integrated with TailwindCSS. The idea is to offer a ton of unstyled components and then with tailwind you customize them. There is still the additional plus that the components are generated within the repo and committed, so no npm package. By doing so we can customize them as we like.

author: intls
body:
***Description***

1. Syntax Error  - A closing curly brace` } `is missing in the f-string on line 41. This results in a syntax error because Python expects the expression inside the curly braces to be completed and the quotation marks to be closed.

2. Type Mismatch - The variables `TEST,` `FETCH`, and `NO_CACHE `are initialized using the `env_vars` function, which returns string values (e.g., `"true"` or `"false"`). However, in the `ExecConf` class, these variables are annotated as `bool`. Assigning string values to boolean attributes leads to a type mismatch.

If the string values are converted to booleans before assignment, this ensures that the `test`, `fetch`, and `no_cache` attributes will have the `bool` type, consistent with their annotations.

author: fabianuntermoser
body:
Currently the navigation command relies on sorting files alphabetically.
This PR adds support for different modes of file sorting.
Fixes #13 

Design considerations:
- Use sort modes already known to Obsidian (alphabetically, by creation and by modification timestamps)
- Add one command for each sort mode, in order to allow assigning specific hotkeys/vimkeys.
- Add one default/global command based on a plugin setting or the file explorer setting.

I didn't find a proper way to access the file explorers sort mode in the Docs. 
However it can be obtained like this: 
`this.app.workspace.getLeavesOfType('file-explorer')[0].view.sortOrder`
(Taken from [File explorer API? - Developers: Plugin & API - Obsidian Forum](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/file-explorer-api/73329))
Working with Obsidian internals like this might break plugin behaviour in future updates. 
Therefore, using solely a setting seems more appropriate. 

Tasks:
- [x] Add sorting alphabetically, by creation and by modification timestamps
- [x] Adds specific navigation commands for each sort mode
  - "Navigate to next alphabetical file" / "Navigate to previous alphabetical file"  
  - "Navigate to next created file" / "Navigate to previous created file"
  - "Navigate to next modified file" / "Navigate to previous modified file"
- [x] Add plugin settings page with dropdown for default sort mode
- [x] Add default navigation command using sort mode defined in plugin settings page
  - "Navigate to next file" and "Navigate to previous file"

body:
---
name: solution review 
about: A template PR for code review with a checklist
---

<!--
  make this PR easy to find:

  - assign: yourself
  - link it to the corresponding challenge issue on the project board
-->

<!-- describe the challenge you will solve -->

## Behavior

### Files

- [ ] The file name describes the function's behavior
- [ ] There is a module docstring in the function file
- [ ] The test file's name matches the function file name -
  `/tests/test_file_name.py`
- [ ] There is a module docstring in the tests file

### Unit Tests

- [ ] The test class has a helpful name in PascalCase
- [ ] The test class has a docstring
- Every unit test has
  - [ ] A helpful name
  - [ ] A clear docstring
  - [ ] Only one assertion
  - [ ] There is no logic in the unit test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] There are tests for defensive assertions
- [ ] There are tests for boundary cases

### Function Docstring

- [ ] The function's behavior is described
- The function's arguments are described:
  - [ ] Type
  - [ ] Purpose
  - [ ] Other assumptions (eg. if it's a number, what's the expected range?)
- The return value is described
  - [ ] Type
  - [ ] Other assumptions are documented
- The defensive assertions are documented using `Raises:`
  - [ ] Each assumption about an argument is checked with an assertion
  - [ ] Each assertion checks for _only one_ assumption about the argument
- [ ] Include 3 or more (passing!) doctests

### The Function

- [ ] The function's name describes it's behavior
- [ ] The function's name matches the file name
- [ ] The function has correct type annotations

## Strategy

### Do's

- [ ] Variable names help to understand the strategy
- [ ] Any comments are clear and describe the strategy
- [ ] Lines of code are spaced to help show different stages of the strategy

### Don'ts

- [ ] The function's strategy _is not_ described in the documentation
- [ ] Comments explain the _strategy_, **not** the _implementation_
- [ ] The function _does not_ have more comments than code
  - If it does, consider finding a new strategy or a simpler implementation

## Implementation

- [ ] The code passes the formatting checks
- [ ] The code passes all Ruff linting checks
- [ ] The code has no (reasonable) Pylint errors
  - In code review, you can decide when fixing a Pylint error is helpful and
    when it's too restricting.
- [ ] Variables are named with snake_case
- [ ] Variable names are clear and helpful
- [ ] The code follows the strategy as simply as possible
- [ ] The implementation is as simple as possible given the strategy
- [ ] The code includes defensive assertions
- [ ] Defensive assertions include as little logic as possible

author: yukawa
body:
## Description
This is a follow up commit to my previous commit (6dadef1c3d456649f8fbe48b6ee1f1515367b5e1), which updated the Bazel version from 7.4.1 to 8.0.0.

 * https://github.com/google/mozc/issues/1118

It turns out that `--noincompatible_enable_cc_toolchain_resolution` is now no-op in Bazel 8.0. Thus there remains no way other than fully migrating to the new CC toolchain resolution as planned.

 * https://github.com/google/mozc/issues/1112

Otherwise `mozc_tip32.dll` will be built as a 64-bit executable.

 * https://github.com/google/mozc/issues/1102

This commit consists of two parts:

 1. explicitly register CC toolchains in `.bazelrc`.
 2. Switch from `--cpu` commandline option to `--platforms` commandline option in `_win_executable_transition`.

With above `mozc_tip32.dll` will be built as a 32-bit executable again.

Closes #1102.
Closes #1112.

## Issue IDs

 * https://github.com/google/mozc/issues/1102
 * https://github.com/google/mozc/issues/1112

## Steps to test new behaviors (if any)
 - OS: Windows 11
 - Steps:
   1. Build `Mozc64.msi` with Bazel
   2. Install `Mozc64.msi`
   3. `dumpbin /headers "C:\Program Files (x86)\Mozc\mozc_tip32.dll" | findstr machine`
   4. Confirm `14C machine (x86)` is shown.

author: larspet
body:
There were many instances where either `EditorNode::load_scene()`/`open_request()` or `load_resource()` was called depending on if the file was a `PackedScene` or not. This PR is meant to simplify those cases and make the `PackedScene` checks more consistent. This also led to some minor bug fixes related to reopening closed scene tabs with the `Ctrl+Shift+T` command.

### Add `EditorNode::load_scene_or_resource()`


I was unsure if I should add this new function, or instead allow `load_resource()` to load scenes as well (instead of simply inspecting the `PackedScene` resource). Additionally, `load_resource()` could then have a new parameter `p_open_if_scene`, deciding between opening or inspecting.

### Remove `EditorNode::open_request()`
`open_request()` did two things:
1. Remove scene from previous scenes list.
2. Call `load_scene()`.

This meant that directly calling `load_scene()` would not update the previous scenes history. I removed `open_request()` and moved the updating of previous scenes  to `load_scene()` instead.

### Refactor previous scenes logic

- Rename related variables/functions to `prev_closed_scenes` to differentiate from `recent_scenes`.
- Enable or disable `FILE_OPEN_PREV` menu_item/shortcut directly when updating previous scene list (instead of just after opening/closing the Scene menu.
- Remove `opening_prev` member variable. It has no purpose and just caused clutter by setting it to `false` everywhere.

author: sasa-tomic
body:
# Features

- **Tabs UI Component**: Introduced a new `TabsState` struct to manage tab navigation within the application. The UI now includes four tabs: **Logs**, **Progress**, **Details**, and **Status**.

- **Progress Tracking**: Implemented a progress tracking mechanism using a `progress` field in the `App` struct to visually indicate the status of operations.

- **Rendering Enhancements**: Added functions to render logs, progress, details, and status messages in the terminal UI, improving user feedback during operations.

# Changes

- **Code Structure**: Refactored the main application logic into separate methods for clarity (e.g., `on_key`, `update_progress`, `add_log`).
- **Terminal Handling**: Improved the handling of terminal states during initialization and shutdown processes, specifically with mouse capture and alternate screen modes.
- **Overall UI Update**: Enhanced terminal UI to provide a more interactive experience with updated interactions and visual elements.

# Cleanup

- **Legacy Code Removed**: Cleaned up old rendering logic related to the previously used message rendering system, transitioning to a more modular approach with dedicated functions for different UI components.

author: ebroder
body:
I'd recommend reading the individual commit messages separately (especially d6eb0e902564fffe6a67c08f497954da4dab0666). For puzzles which required markup changes in order to copy-paste cleanly, I enabled each of them in a separate commit with an explanation for the required changes.

~~As a note, this will not on its own cause copy-pasting of images to work from dev, because dev requires authentication for all URLs, and Google Sheets proxies image requests.~~ (I've pushed a commit to address this). For similar reasons, copy-paste from localhost doesn't really work for images. However, Sheets will still paste in the correctly constructed formulas, so you can confirm that the right thing is happening on our side. I'm going to work on un-authenticating `/static` (similar to how we do for staging), but didn't want to block this PR on that.

Once we're happy with this, I'll also start working through the backlog of puzzles that are already typeset. That'll probably include some revisions for common components (e.g. `Crossword`). The [2024 code](https://github.com/ttbnl-2024/mitmh-2024-pre-posthunt/blob/main/client/components/copy.tsx) has a bunch of embedded top-level logic for handling crosswords, blanks, etc., but my hope is that any remaining idiosyncrasies can be handled per-component using `COPY_ONLY_CLASS` and/or `NO_COPY_CLASS`.

Sending @zarvox the main review, but CC'ing @als364 as an FYI since I tweaked a handful of your puzzles.

Edit your `online-botique-params.yaml` file and commit the changes to your repository. Make sure that you commit the changes to the path and branch in the repository that are specified in the deployment file.

The replace the iframe with a "gateway page" which summarizes the PDF and let's the user decide if they want to take the trouble to view or download it. The link is styled as a button to ensure it is distinct from regular links. It also has text indicating the link is to a PDF,  the file size, and that the link will open in a new tab. These are all accessibility features.

author: felixwrt
body:
I'm using the `fritzapi` crate to read data from a FRITZ!Dect 210 smart plug and my program stopped working a couple of weeks ago. The root cause seems to be that with the latest firmware, the `productname` reported by the device changed such that it isn't recognized by fritzapi anymore.

Here's how the device is reported:

```
Device {
    ...
    fwversion: "04.27",
    manufacturer: "AVM",
    productname: "FRITZ!Smart Energy 210",
    ...
}
```

The change is intentional and also in the official release notes: https://en.avm.de/service/update-news/?product=fritzdect-210

> FRITZ!DECT 210 was renamed to FRITZ!Smart Energy 210

This PR changes the device detection logic such that the new product name is also recognized as being a `FritzDect2XX`.

Let me know if you have questions.

body:
## Description
This PR adds a new LLM Router component that intelligently routes queries to the most appropriate language model based on OpenRouter specifications and task requirements.

## Features
- Automatic model specification fetching from OpenRouter API
- Dynamic model selection based on task complexity and requirements
- Multiple optimization modes (quality, speed, cost, balanced)
- Robust error handling with fallback mechanisms

## Usage
1. Connect multiple LLM models to the router
2. Add a judge LLM for selection
3. Provide input message
4. Select optimization preference
5. Router will automatically select and use the most appropriate model

# Enhance Git-ACP with Ollama Integration and Debug Output

## Summary

This PR introduces Ollama integration for AI-powered commit message generation and adds a new formatting module for consistent debug output. It includes significant refactoring of the codebase to improve modularity, error handling, and debugging capabilities.

---

## Files Changed

### Added

1. **`git_acp/formatting.py`**  
   - New module for centralized formatting and debug output
   - Implements color constants and consistent formatting functions
   - Provides reusable components for status messages and debug information

2. **`tests/__init__.py`**  
   - Package initialization for tests

3. **`tests/test_ai_utils.py`**  
   - Test suite for AI utilities module
   - Covers commit message generation and system prompt creation

4. **`tests/test_git_operations.py`**  
   - Comprehensive test suite for git operations
   - Tests all core git functionality with mocked subprocess calls

### Modified

1. **`git_acp/ai_utils.py`**  
   - Refactored to use Ollama's Python client instead of subprocess
   - Split functionality into smaller, focused functions
   - Added verbose debug output support
   - Improved error handling and context gathering

2. **`git_acp/git_operations.py`**  
   - Added config parameter for verbose output
   - Improved error handling and debugging
   - Updated to use new formatting module
   - Fixed commit data handling and reference issues

3. **`requirements.txt`**  
   - Added `ollama` package for AI integration
   - Added `tqdm` for potential progress bars
   - Reorganized dependencies

---

## Code Changes

### `git_acp/formatting.py`

```python
# Color constants for easy customization
DEBUG_HEADER_COLOR = "blue"
DEBUG_VALUE_COLOR = "cyan"
SUCCESS_COLOR = "green"
WARNING_COLOR = "yellow"
STATUS_COLOR = "bold green"

def debug_header(message: str) -> None:
    """Print a debug header message."""
    rprint(f"[{DEBUG_HEADER_COLOR}]Debug - {message}[{DEBUG_HEADER_COLOR}]")

def debug_item(label: str, value: str = None) -> None:
    """Print a debug item with optional value."""
    if value is not None:
        rprint(f"[{DEBUG_HEADER_COLOR}]  • {label}:[{DEBUG_HEADER_COLOR}] [{DEBUG_VALUE_COLOR}]{value}[{DEBUG_VALUE_COLOR}]")
```

- Centralized formatting logic with customizable colors
- Consistent debug output formatting
- Reusable components for all output types

---

## Reason for Changes

1. **AI Integration Improvement**
   - Switched to Ollama's Python client for better reliability
   - Added proper error handling and context management
   - Improved commit message generation with better context

2. **Debug Output Enhancement**
   - Added verbose mode with detailed debug information
   - Centralized formatting for consistency
   - Made debug output more readable and informative

3. **Code Quality**
   - Added comprehensive test suites
   - Improved error handling throughout
   - Better separation of concerns

---

## Impact of Changes

### Positive Impacts

- More reliable AI-powered commit message generation
- Better debugging capabilities with `-v` flag
- Consistent and readable debug output
- Improved code maintainability
- Comprehensive test coverage

### Potential Issues

- New dependency on `ollama` package
- Requires Ollama service to be running for AI features
- Slightly increased memory usage due to debug output formatting

---

## Test Plan

1. **Unit Testing**  
   - Added comprehensive test suites for both AI utilities and git operations
   - Tests cover all core functionality with mocked dependencies
   - Includes error handling and edge cases

2. **Integration Testing**  
   - Test AI integration with actual Ollama service
   - Verify debug output formatting in different scenarios
   - Test git operations with actual repository

3. **Manual Testing**  
   ```bash
   # Test basic functionality
   python -m git_acp
   
   # Test with verbose output
   python -m git_acp -v
   
   # Test AI integration
   python -m git_acp -o
   ```

---

## Additional Notes

- The formatting module is designed to be easily customizable through color constants
- Debug output can be extended by adding new formatting functions as needed
- Consider adding more AI models or services in the future
- May want to add configuration options for debug output colors

I tried the newly introduced amd gpu monitoring from https://github.com/corecoding/Vitals/pull/456 and noticed the displayed memory values are not correct. For my  RX 7800 XT this was displayed (with decimal setting)

![before-fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a611eb2-356f-468b-8201-5af61db7f6d2)

17TB would not be bad but sadly this card only has 16GB of memory 😉 With this change the reporting will show the following

**decimal**

**binary**
![after-fix-binary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8ac7c47-a5eb-495c-ba23-202717a7505f)

Grabbing the memory-measurment setting is not optimal but needs to be done for correct unit calculation. Best would be to pass the unit of the measurement with the reading but this would be a bigger rework.

author: mschilling
body:
This pull request introduces several updates to the user management functionality and refactors some utilities in the codebase. The changes include improvements to the user controller, the addition of data transformation utilities, and updates to the user service and data models.

### User Management Enhancements:

* [`apps/api/src/controllers/users-controller.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-acb41a21c6977cafb7b284ec2dacbbb842c5d9316dd7bb2e5674b0dcdc926037L1-R41): Refactored the user controller to separate the routes for fetching a single user and multiple users. Added data transformation using `UserDto` for consistent API responses.
* [`apps/api/src/core/dto/user.dto.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-660860d1a900ae0abaa3738673f481f65a68d714f125c8b8f2f3792337744c93R1-R24): Introduced `UserDto` class with properties to expose user data in a structured format.

### Utility Functions:

* [`apps/api/src/core/utils/transformer.utils.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-264d90a9f64934b55bca06276649df1fece0a72710710534fbad9a0346133aa1R1-R18): Added utility functions `transformTo` and `transformArrayTo` for converting plain objects to instances of classes with data transformation capabilities.
* [`libs/common/src/utils/time/time.utils.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-8ed32ffd3b7bf122463e4d6e6f211ca377bdb25d0b24285be7cf9324624dbf0bR1-R5): Added `getCurrentTimeAsISO` utility function to get the current time in ISO format.

### User Service and Data Models:

* [`libs/common/src/services/user.service.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-a6493abab5abe90093795414d53d37ba0877be0e2e9986a373f86349f67aad69L1-R5): Updated the `UserService` to include pagination support and to use the new `userConverter` for Firestore data conversion.
* [`libs/common/src/models.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-e11aaf2690a1555a400cebba048c0333ca2c8367c8bdf88f1dd6ffe735ddcbc1L6-R16): Modified the `User` interface to use string types for `createdAt` and `lastLogin` fields instead of `Timestamp`.

These changes collectively enhance the user management functionality by improving data handling, consistency, and introducing better utility functions for data transformation.

author: frenzibyte
body:
- Moves `NSString`/`NSImage` conversion methods away from `Cocoa` class
- Defines `NSString` and uses `stringWithCharacters:length:` rather than `alloc` & `initWithCharacters:length:` 
  - General rule of thumb in Objective-C to never use `alloc` and `init` if there's a "convenient constructor" available.
- Uses `LibraryImport` instead of `DllImport` (optional but why not)
- Moves code that can be shared with iOS to a different namespace and renames `Cocoa` to `Interop`.

I've also explored the path of using native SDKs offered by .NET but it was not a simple change and a lot needs to be reconsidered, so I'm not looking into that any further at the moment.

author: domkirby
body:
Merging the 3.0.0 code to the ``latest`` branch. Features include:
- Encryption keys are now derived _per secret_ using the secret's ID and ``PBKDF2``
- The ``SERVER_SIDE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`` constant is deprecated because it is no longer used to encrypt secrets.
- Adds option for ``PBKDF2_ITERATIONS`` to ``_config.php`` and defaults to ``100000``. This is only for iterations on the server side encryption.
- Adds option for ``MAXIMUM_VIEWS`` to ``_config.php`` and defaults to ``5``. Creates client side and server side validation to prevent a secret from having too many views based on preference.

## BREAKING CHANGES
- Old secrets will no longer be accessible upon deployment!
- Fills exists in ``index.php`` for the new constants, so repulling ``_config.php`` is recommended but not required. Be sure to preserve your database information and other settings if you merge ``_config.php``!

body:
This commit enhances the server shutdown test with more reliable synchronization and error handling. Key improvements include:

- Refactored `NewTestServer` to set up the server more completely
- Rewrote `TestServerShutdown` to directly test server shutdown mechanism
- Improved error handling and synchronization during server stop
- Removed unused synchronization channel
- Added more detailed logging for test diagnostics

Changes address flaky test behavior by:
- Using explicit server listener start
- Utilizing server.Shutdown() with a context
- Handling potential errors more robustly
- Ensuring proper server stoppage verification

The test now more accurately simulates real-world server shutdown scenarios and provides better visibility into the shutdown process.

Fixes intermittent test failures in server shutdown test

- Making it easier to update blockchain functionality independently
- Reducing core firmware complexity

author: brimoor
body:
Adds a `create_index` kwarg to `GeoNear` and `GeoWithin` stages, for consistency with the `SortBy` and `GroupBy` stages.

Note that, unlike sorting/grouping, the geo stages **require** the spherical index to exist in order to function. However, it feels appropriate to provide a `create_index=False` syntax to provide users a way to guarantee that nothing expensive like index creation will occur when creating/using a view.

author: hectickiwi
body:
### Description

If you start a tier list, then go back and start another tier list, data gets carried over unexpectedly.

The cause is that when initializing a tier list, a shallow copy of the `DEFAULT_TIER_TEMPLATE` is used. When you edit the tier list, it ends up mutating the template tiers, which causes these edits to carry over to the next tier list you start.

Fixed by using a deep copy of `DEFAULT_TIER_TEMPLATE`.

author: sambhav
body:
This pull request includes several significant changes to the `cloudcoil` project, primarily focusing on restructuring directories, updating dependencies, and refining code for better clarity and functionality. The most important changes include renaming directories, updating Python versions, and modifying import statements and class definitions.

### Directory and File Structure Updates:
* Renamed the `cloudcoil/models` directory to `cloudcoil/kinds` and moved `cloudcoil/models/apimachinery/v1.py` to `cloudcoil/apimachinery.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L29-R36) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b77e95e9e9ee74eb756ff07bdcdf7a96b1e127f86589c0230f621e711c4379e3L7-R20).

### Dependency and Version Updates:
* Updated the Python version target from 3.9 to 3.10 in the `Makefile` and changed the output directory for generated models.

### Import Statement Updates:
* Updated import paths in `README.md` to reflect the new directory structure (`cloudcoil.kinds` instead of `cloudcoil.models`).
* Added `ResourceList` to the imports in `cloudcoil/client/__init__.py` and `Makefile` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4057ef0fe8860290f3edae2ccc8c19ded5c3e67bdebbe978ef5a210be18b0a53L3-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L46-R50).

### Code Refinements:
* Replaced assertions with explicit checks for `metadata.name` in `cloudcoil/client/_api_client.py` to raise `ValueError` if not set [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-003c287eabfb30f1d5ac7eab59dcc0603f8d6e6c45e7554828113dfffcdb8066L75-R74) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-003c287eabfb30f1d5ac7eab59dcc0603f8d6e6c45e7554828113dfffcdb8066L89-R88) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-003c287eabfb30f1d5ac7eab59dcc0603f8d6e6c45e7554828113dfffcdb8066L116-R115).
* Removed redundant imports and updated type annotations in `cloudcoil/apimachinery.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b77e95e9e9ee74eb756ff07bdcdf7a96b1e127f86589c0230f621e711c4379e3L332-R331) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b77e95e9e9ee74eb756ff07bdcdf7a96b1e127f86589c0230f621e711c4379e3L447-L496).

### Testing Updates:
* Renamed the `test_clientset` fixture to `test_client_set` in `cloudcoil/_testing/plugin.py` for consistency.
